name: La Carcasa

location.address: Jardi Botanic de la Universitat de Valencia, Carrer Quart 80, 46008 Valencia

verified_sources: data/registers/valencia-arboles-monumentales.json (register_id 4916, Generalitat Valenciana Catalogo de Arboles Monumentales)
access: Paid entry to the Jardi Botanic (small fee), the same garden as several already-published trees (Kashmir Cypress, Caucasian Elm, Bottle Tree and others).
transport: 10 min walk from Angel Guimera metro station
verify_notes: Register (Generalitat Valenciana Catalogo de Arboles Monumentales, register_id 4916) lists this Phoenix dactylifera at 39.47774,-0.386057, height 19.1m, no girth recorded (null in register, plausible for a multi-trunked specimen where a single girth figure would be misleading). Independently confirmed by the Jardi Botanic de la Universitat de Valencia's own site (jardibotanic.org), which names it 'la palmera mas especial del Jardin' and says it has more than 35 branches/trunks, a form that resembles the frame of a firework shell casing ('carcasa' in Spanish), which is where the name comes from. OSM polygon check: register coordinates fall inside the Jardi Botanic's mapped boundary (way 10115902), consistent with the other Botanic Garden trees already published (vlc_010, vlc_015, vlc_017-vlc_022, vlc_025), so this is the same cluster and adds to an already-open garden rather than opening a new location. No age found in any source; leave age_estimate empty and let the page ask the reader. No girth to derive an age from either. What makes it remarkable: unlike almost every date palm, which grows a single trunk, this one branches into 35+ separate stems from a shared base, a genuinely unusual and visually striking form worth seeing in person; the Cadiz-standard photo test (fills the frame, readable crown and trunk) would be easy to pass here given the distinctive silhouette.
